t.E574.agn: In 1998, JECFA set a group ADI 'not specified' for glucono-delta-lactone and the calcium, magnesium, potassium and sodium salts of gluconic acid. JECFA reported that single doses of glucono-delta-lactone above 20 g had a laxative effect in humans and that diarrhoea was reported in volunteers taking 20–50 g per day. EFSA's re-evaluation in the EU is ongoing (a new call for data was made in 2023).
t.E574.body: Gluconic acid and its salts are normal intermediates formed in the body during the breakdown of glucose via the pentose phosphate pathway; part of the ingested gluconate is excreted unchanged in urine, and the rest is broken down.
t.E574.eff.0.a: Above 20 g in a single dose; in volunteers taking 20–50 g per day
t.E574.eff.0.t: Laxative effect; diarrhoea has been reported
t.E574.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E574.prod: It is produced by fermentation of glucose.
t.E574.regx.0: No separate ADI for gluconic acid; group ADI 'not specified' for glucono-delta-lactone, with which it is in equilibrium in water, and for gluconate salts.
t.E574.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E574.regx.2: Re-evaluation ongoing; a call for data was made in 2023 (deadline 31.03.2024).
t.E574.summary: A mild acid obtained from glucose. Used as an acidity regulator.
t.E574.what: It is a mild organic acid obtained from glucose, used as an acidity regulator and raising agent. In water it is in equilibrium with glucono-delta-lactone.
